title: EAP: support use of nested TLS decoding and fix EAPOL/TLS decoding
description:
The nested TLS work (https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24261 and https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24945) which this is based upon, allows us to clean up the EAP dissector.

Included in this work is fixing TLS decoding for EAPOL, as well as improving conversation tracking when the PAE multicast group address is used in both directors as the destination MAC addresses.

Conversation topics:
 * I had to make the TLS dissector `use_conv_addr_port_endpoints` aware as it otherwise directly uses `pinfo->{src,dst,srcport,destport}` and rewriting them effects the display output
    * I need guidance on what a better approach looks like.
    * this more than likely breaks something, though there are very few users of `conversation_set_conv_addr_port_endpoints()` (TLS wise at a glance only `packet-eap.c` and potentially `packet-proxy.c`)
    * I moved `struct conversation_addr_port_endpoints` into `conversation.h` only to show for this approach the contents of this needs exposing to `packet-tls-utils.c`; if this is probably the least awful way I'll create a set of 'get_endpoint_src()`-esque helpers
    * My only other thought is to use the approach of `p_{get,set}_proto_depth` to smuggle a hint to TLS from keyed off `session->app_handle` on if this frame is a 'server' for `ssl_packet_from_server` to use; though maybe we need full addr/port for all the other parts of the TLS dissector that use `pinfo->{dst,src,srcport,destport}` 
    * ~I have not edited yet DTLS as I suspect my current approach needs to be replaced~
 * ~using `curr_layer_num` instead of `curr_proto_layer_num` for my nested EAP partitioning; maybe an effect of using `tls_set_appdata_dissector` doing things differently?~
    * moved to `p_{get,set}_proto_depth` as recommended by @johnthacker in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24261#note_3330008756
 * ~not sure if the backfill of the seemingly missing nested TLS hooks is needed; should probably be further discussed in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/work_items/21027~
    * ~nested TLS merged, no longer necessary except for the missed plumbing fixed by https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24945~

EAP: use wmem_map to partition conversation tracking by p_{get,set}_proto_depth

This commit also includes fixes for conversation tracking for EAPOL which
uses multicast, allowing for TLS decoding there too.
